datasets.name: StudentLife (original Dartmouth release)
notes: The item with usable density is Stress, but its documented options are “1 a little stressed, 2 definitely stressed, 3 stressed out, 4 feeling good, 5 feeling great”. The numbers are not ordered by stress, so an ordinal model fitted to them is fitting a scale that does not exist. The loader remaps them by label text, which fixes the ordering but cannot create more data.
Even after recovering malformed records and applying that remap, only 1 participant has 60 or more responses in both halves of their own span. The screen needs at least 10.

This does not depend on the number 60. Sweeping the per-window minimum from 20 to 100 across three window rules, StudentLife reaches 10 qualifying participants only at 20-30 per window — a threefold relaxation of the pre-specified rule, which would leave a five-category probit slope fitted to roughly 20 points per person.

Every properly ordered alternative item is far sparser than Stress: Behavior/anxious: 43 participants, median 4 responses each, most 75 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs; Behavior/calm: 42 participants, median 4 responses each, most 75 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs; Sleep/rate: 49 participants, median 25 responses each, most 73 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs; Social/number: 48 participants, median 22 responses each, most 79 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs; Activity/working: 46 participants, median 8 responses each, most 39 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs; Exercise/exercise: 46 participants, median 11 responses each, most 44 — 0 reach the 120 the screen needs.

About 10% of Stress records in the original archive store the answer under a literal “null” key rather than “level”, and that key also holds GPS strings. Those are recovered when the value is a digit in range and discarded when it is a coordinate.
Stored codes are NOT in severity order; the remap reorders them by label text.
Read the [9b] association-strength diagnostic before interpreting any estimate.
exclusion_reasons: only 1 participants have >= 120 matched reports (60 per epoch); the primary analysis needs at least 10.
